both.statement: Seven is a rummy-style card game.
both.quotedFromA: Seven is a card game in the rummy style.
both.quotedFromB: Seven is a rummy-style card game.

both.statement: The game supports 1 player at minimum.
both.quotedFromA: The game supports 1 player at minimum.

both.statement: The game supports up to 7 players at maximum.
both.quotedFromA: The game supports up to 7 players at maximum.

both.statement: A single game takes roughly 7 minutes to play.
both.quotedFromA: A single game takes roughly 7 minutes to play.

both.statement: Each player receives one "Ways to Score" card during setup.

both.quotedFromB: Each player receives a Ways to Score card during setup.

both.quotedFromB: Each player draws 3 cards from the center pool during setup to form their initial hand.

both.statement: Each player draws 2 cards into their hand each round.
both.quotedFromA: In a round, each player draws two cards into their hand.
both.quotedFromB: Each player draws 2 cards into their hand each round.

both.statement: Each player discards 1 card from their hand each round.

both.quotedFromB: Each player discards 1 card from their hand each round.

both.quotedFromA: Discard piles are public information that any player may inspect.

both.statement: At the end of the game, each player has 7 discards.

both.quotedFromB: At game end, a player will have accumulated 7 discards.

both.quotedFromB: The game ends when all players have 10 cards in hand.

both.statement: Each player scores their best hand of 7 cards.

both.quotedFromB: Each player scores their best hand of 7 cards.

both.statement: Bonus point cards add to a player's score even beyond the scoring hand of 7.
both.quotedFromA: Bonus point cards add to a player's score even if they are not part of the scoring seven-card hand.
both.quotedFromB: Players add bonus point cards beyond their scoring hand to their score.

both.quotedFromA: A match is made up of seven games.
both.quotedFromB: A match consists of 7 games of Seven.

both.statement: Players keep track of each player's cumulative score total across the games of the match.
both.quotedFromA: Players record each player's cumulative score across the seven games of the match.
both.quotedFromB: Players keep track of each player's score total across all games.

both.statement: The player with the highest total score at the end of the match wins.
both.quotedFromA: The player with the highest cumulative score when the match ends wins the match.
both.quotedFromB: The player with the highest total score at the end of the match wins.

both.statement: Players may play a shorter match as a best of 3 games.
both.quotedFromA: Players may shorten a match to a best-of-three series if they prefer.
both.quotedFromB: Shorter matches can be played as a best of 3 games.

both.statement: Players may play a longer match as a best of 10 games.
both.quotedFromA: Players may lengthen a match to a best-of-ten series if they prefer.
both.quotedFromB: Longer matches can be played as a best of 10 games.

aOnly.statement: Setup creates a face-down, shuffled-around pile of cards (the mess) in the center of the table.
aOnly.sourceSentence: Create a mess of face-down cards in the middle of the table and mixes them around.

aOnly.statement: Rounds are played simultaneously by all players.
A player's discard count tells them which round they are on.
aOnly.sourceSentence: If you ever lose track of which round you are on, count your discards, you will have 7 discards when the game is over.

aOnly.statement: The round-end check is whether every player holds ten cards: if so the game ends, otherwise another round begins.
aOnly.sourceSentence: If everyone has 10 cards, end the game; otherwise begin the next round.

aOnly.statement: The default match format is a best-of-seven series.
aOnly.sourceSentence: A full match of Seven is naturally played in a best of 7 series.

bOnly.statement: Discarded cards are placed face-up off to the side of the table in each player's own discard pile.
bOnly.sourceSentence: Each player discards 1 card from their hand face-up off to the side of the table in their own discard pile.

derivedLineProposals.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): The round structure is draw 2 / discard 1, netting +1 card per round; starting at 3 cards and ending at 10 cards means 7 rounds, matching the 7 discards stated as the count at game end.

derivedLineProposals.arithmeticNote: Net cards gained per round = draw(2) - discard(1) = 1. Span of hand size growth = end(10) - start(3) = 7. Rounds = span(7) / net(1) = 7. This computed round count of 7 also matches the independently stated fact that each player has 7 discards at game end.
